results.title: Non-Convex Optimization with Spectral Radius Regularization
results.content:
Title: Non-Convex Optimization with Spectral Radius Regularization
Thus, in practice, optimal machine learning models near flatter optima should perform better than those near sharper minima on test data distributed differently than the original training data Keskar et al., [2017]. Therefore, by regularizing the optimization of models with respect to this spectral radius, we can obtain solutions that are less susceptible to errors and biases in training or test data. Though they experimentally showed that their regularization method has a small generalization gap (between the training and test set), their method also had a higher Hessian spectral radius than vanilla SGD, weight-decay, and adversarial methods. We tested our spectral radius regularization algorithms on the following data sets: forest cover types Blackard and Dean, [1999], United States Postal Service (USPS) handwritten digits LeCun et al., [1990], and chest X-rays Wang et al., [2017]. To test if models with lower spectral radii generalize better than those with higher spectral radii, we created test sets that are differently distributed from the training data. For the chest X-ray models, we compared performance on two similar transfer learning data sets, CheXpert Irvin et al., [2019] and MIMIC-CXR Johnson et al., [2019] (using the six conditions common to all three data sets). We trained a feed-forward neural network on forest cover-type data and compared the accuracy of models on the randomly shifted test sets. Per Figure 1, while the models performed comparably on the test data (all models have an accuracy of 94.47-95.91%), our regularized models (both power iteration and LOBPCG) performed significantly better than the unregularized model on both augmented test data sets (87.10-91.08% vs. Figure 3 shows that the two models with the lowest spectral radius , our regularized model ( and ) and entropy-SGD, performed best on the transfer learning chest X-ray data sets. However, optimal performance requires tuning the regularization parameters and to balance the loss and spectral radius terms, a data- and model-dependent process. Table 6: There is more overlap in the explanations from the two models with low spectral radius (our spectral radius regularization and entropy-SGD) on the CheXpert Validation data set. In contrast, the three models with higher spectral radius, unregularized, K-FAC, and asymmetric valley, have a higher performance drop on the transfer learning data sets and have less overlap in their explanations.

results.title: [2411.06180] Mean Field Control by Stochastic Koopman Operator via a Spectral Method
results.content: [Submitted on 9 Nov 2024]. # Title:Mean Field Control by Stochastic Koopman Operator via a Spectral Method. Authors:Yuhan Zhao, Juntao Chen, Yingdong Lu, Quanyan Zhu. View a PDF of the paper titled Mean Field Control by Stochastic Koopman Operator via a Spectral Method, by Yuhan Zhao and Juntao Chen and Yingdong Lu and Quanyan Zhu. > Abstract:Mean field control provides a robust framework for coordinating large-scale populations with complex interactions and has wide applications across diverse fields. There is a pressing need for data-driven methodologies to construct accurate models and facilitate efficient planning and control. > To this end, we leverage Koopman operator theory to advance solution methods for mean field control problems. Our approach involves exploring stochastic Koopman operators using spectral analysis techniques. Through Koopman decomposition, we derive a linear model for mean field control problems in a data-driven fashion. Finally, we develop a model predictive control framework to achieve robust control and reduce the computational complexity for mean field control problems, thereby enhancing the efficacy and applicability of mean field control solutions in various domains. **[v1]** Sat, 9 Nov 2024 13:45:10 UTC (70 KB). ## Access Paper:. results.title: Random vibration analysis of a ring model based on a modal cross-spectral density - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Full Length Article Random vibration analysis of a ring model based on a modal cross-spectral density. The cross-spectral density (Cross-SD; CSD) can be used to explore the relationship between random input forces and responses in the frequency domain. In this study, the frequency response function, autocorrelation function, and SD are defined for a unit force harmonic input based on Gaussian white noise applied to the ring structure. In this study, a novel method is presented to advance vibration engineering by extending the SD model of beams to ring structures. Random vibration analysis is crucial in oscillation testing and inspection, as it determines the frequencies of a structure. [6,7] first studied thermoelastic damping (TED) of silicon micro-rings with rectangular cross-section, and Li et al. Additionally, numerous studies have been conducted on the random vibration analysis of ring models. Modal analysis is a technique for analyzing vibration response to external forces in terms of eigenfrequencies [20] and is used in various fields, including mechanical, aerospace, and civil engineering. Considering the prior topics, the analysis of the antiresonant frequency and SD of the ring model represents a promising research area that has not been pioneered yet. For this purpose, a novel vibration analysis method is presented utilizing CSD in ring structures. This work aims to provide an in-depth insight into the vibration response characteristics by analyzing the SD based on “Gaussian white noise”, which is assumed to be the most common normal distribution at the resonant and antiresonant frequencies of the ring. This study introduces SD as an autocorrelation function to analyze the vibrational response of a ring model. In this section, the spectral density (SD) in random vibration is first defined, and the equation for the ring is introduced for in-plane vibration modes. Random vibration analysis is performed on the free boundary condition ring with radius *a*, stiffness *EI*, linear damping coefficient *c*, material density , sectional area *A*, and Poisson’s ratio , as shown. This study analyzed the effect of external force vibration on the arbitrary excitation of a ring. Employing Hamilton's principle within the continuous flexibility framework, this work develops a novel theoretical dynamic model to investigate the vibration characteristics of cracked bearing rings.
